news.title: Xavi Hernandez All Set To Lead Dutch FIFA World Cup Dream Following Netherlands Appointment
news.lede: Star Spanish football manager Xavi Hernandez is set to lead the Dutch FIFA World Cup dream, after he was appointed the head coach of the Netherlands men’s football team on a four-year contract on Wednesday. Xavi takes over from Ronald Koeman, who stepped down after the Netherlands’ last-32 exit to Morocco at this summer’s FIFA World Cup. A World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, Xavi also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and 2012. He started his managerial career with Qatari club Al Sadd before guiding Barcelona to the La Liga title in 2023.

news.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
news.lede: Messi’s father, ⁠Jorge, died last week at age of 68. Argentinian suggests he may not play on much longer. Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father. Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

news.title: Malawi's Historic World Cup Journey: A Testament to FIFA's African Investment
news.lede: Malawi's unprecedented qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup is credited to FIFA's investment in African football under President Gianni Infantino. The country's Football Association President, Fleetwood Haiya, asserts that Infantino's focus on leveling the playing field has been instrumental in their success. Haiya praises Infantino for prioritizing football development in undervalued associations, citing the decision to withdraw proposals that could detract from supporting poorer member associations. His unwavering loyalty to Infantino is based on shared values, promoting grassroots and women's football across Malawi.
